newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bourse raps Handelsbanken, Pen-Sam. [CORRECTED 14:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Danish bourse raps Handelsbanken, Pen-Sam. [CORRECTED 14:25 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline from "Danish bourse raps Handelsbanken, Mols-Linien." changing company being reprimanded by the bourse.)

The Copenhagen Stock Exchange on Wednesday reprimanded Swedish bank Svenska Handelsbanken and Danish pension fund Pen-Sam for rigging the price of shares in ferry operator Mols-Linien A/S and said it had called in the regulators.

"On 30 December 1996, Pen-Sam and Svenska Handelsbanken concluded transactions in Mols-Linien's share with the sole purpose of influencing the official price of that share on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange," a bourse statement said.
"The stock exchange is of the opinion that price manipulation as defined in the Danish Securities Trading Act has occurred," it added.
"Consequently the stock exchange has requested the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority to institute an inquiry into the matter," the bourse said.

It said that it would exclude six transactions on December 30 from the official calculation of Mols-Linien prices and the revised official prices for the day were now 260 crowns broker-to-broker and 263 for all trades.
